matches.rationale: Both identify that the abstract's claim about Memory Mosaics v2 trained on 1T tokens outperforming a transformer trained on 8T tokens is exaggerated; pred_id 6 specifically references Table 5 (46.9% vs 53.4%) and Section 6 evidence, capturing the same overstated superiority.
No finding addresses the adaptive bandwidth formula inconsistency (sign of β vs. bandwidth relationship).
The identical average (52.2%) for two models in Table 1 is not discussed; findings focus on Table 1 vs Table 2 average discrepancies, not this masking of performance differences.
No finding mentions the asymmetric prompt optimization protocol or possible unequal prompt engineering effort.
The misleading 'successful extrapolation' claim and the severe performance drop (59.3% to 26.5%) are not noted in any finding.
No finding identifies the fabricated or erroneous citation (Zhang, 2025 with impossible year 2504).

The FLOPs/token calculation at context length 256 concealing long-context cost is not captured by any finding; Table 2-related findings concern average discrepancies, not computational cost reporting.
No finding addresses the contradiction between claimed absence of hyperparameter search and Memory Mosaics v2-specific learnable parameters in Table 6.
The oversimplification of transformer degradation in Figure 3 is not discussed in any finding.
No finding mentions the missing data provenance, licensing, or ethical transparency issues.
The abstract's overgeneralised claim of 'significantly outperforming' across all inference-time tasks, contradicted by near-identical persistent-knowledge results, is not raised.
No finding notes the promotional, marketing-style language in the introduction.
The selective reporting of transformer results as '×' at 64k in Table 4 is not addressed by any finding.
The omitted weight matrix dimensionality in Equation (8) is not discussed; pred_id 8 concerns normalisation/gating, not missing dimensions.

Pred_id 6 argues that the claim that increasing data for transformers cannot replicate Memory Mosaics v2's performance is overstated, citing Section 6 evidence that 8× more data does close the gap; this matches the ground-truth issue that the conclusion ignores confounding variables and overstates data scaling limitations.
No finding questions the use of classification accuracy without calibration metrics or justification in the in-context learning evaluation.
The misattribution of the associative memory–attention connection as a novel contribution is not identified in any finding.
No finding points out the contradiction between the Discussion's future direction on reducing long-context computational cost and earlier claims of successful extrapolation.
